registry_objects.title: Constructive Encoding via ABCD
registry_objects.summary: Constructive pairing and sequence encoding via prime powers, without importing set theory. Goedel numbering is a special case of the ABCD encoding (with C=1, D=1).

registry_objects.title: Stages from Limit
registry_objects.summary: The interior is determined by the boundary: two tower-coherent functions with the same boundary data (agreement at a reference depth) have the same interior values at all coarser stages.

registry_objects.title: No Identity Decoherence
registry_objects.summary: No Identity Decoherence: the diagonal resonance pattern (L+E+P) cannot occur at the ontic level in tau, because K5 blocks (L), NF-Confluence blocks (E), and the star-autonomous structure blocks (P).

registry_objects.title: NF Deduplication Invariant
registry_objects.summary: Address DAG construction is deduplication-invariant: identifying shared branches produces the same DAG regardless of order. Follows from Hyperfactorization uniqueness. NF-level analogue of NF-Confluence.

registry_objects.title: Five Generators
registry_objects.summary: The five generators {alpha, pi, gamma, eta, omega} with canonical roles: radial seed, prime base, exponent channel, tetration channel, fixed-point absorber.

registry_objects.title: Progression Operator rho
registry_objects.summary: The sole ontic operator rho: acts as successor within each orbit ray. No other operation creates objects.

registry_objects.title: Diagonal Discipline
registry_objects.summary: Structural principle preventing free contraction/reuse; forces exactly four orbit channels via three successive diagonal rewirings.

registry_objects.title: Static Kernel tau_0
registry_objects.summary: tau_0 = the static kernel: 5 generator objects + K1-K6 axioms + rho. The complete specification before the generative act.

registry_objects.title: Orbit Rays
registry_objects.summary: O_alpha, O_pi, O_gamma, O_eta: the four orbit rays unfolded by rho from each non-omega generator.

registry_objects.title: Iterator Ladder
registry_objects.summary: The operator ladder: rho (raw iteration) -> mu (multiplication) -> nu (exponentiation) -> theta (tetration).

registry_objects.title: tau-Idx (Earned Natural Numbers)
registry_objects.summary: tau-Idx := O_alpha = {alpha, rho(alpha), rho^2(alpha), ...}. The alpha-orbit IS the internal natural numbers (N is not imported but earned).

registry_objects.title: Rank Transfer Maps
registry_objects.summary: For each generator s in {pi, gamma, eta}, RT_s : tau-Idx -> O_s maps rho^n(alpha) to rho^n(s). Canonical bijection between counting scaffold and typed orbit ray.

registry_objects.title: Swap Operator sigma
registry_objects.summary: sigma (swap): first derived operator from rho. Exchanges positions within orbit rays via rank transfer composition.

registry_objects.title: Index Addition
registry_objects.summary: n + m = rho^m(n): addition on tau-Idx earned by iterating rho m times starting from n. No Peano axioms imported.

registry_objects.title: Polarity Pairing
registry_objects.summary: Pairing function Pair: P_tau^+ x P_tau^- -> Z measuring rank distance between B-dominant and C-dominant primes. Consecutive polarity pairs exist infinitely often.

registry_objects.title: PolStream
registry_objects.summary: PolStream(omega): infinite binary sequence recording channel dominance along the primorial spine. At each stage k, records whether prime p_k is B-dominant or C-dominant.

registry_objects.title: Tau-Weighted Boundary Constants
registry_objects.summary: pi_tau := pi * iota_tau and e_tau := e * iota_tau: tau-weighted boundary constants for the two lemniscate lobes. pi_tau + e_tau = 2*iota_tau. Ratio pi_tau/e_tau = pi/e encodes lobe asymmetry.

registry_objects.title: Tau-Bayesian State
registry_objects.summary: A tau-Bayesian state S: Obj(tau) -> [0,1]_tau satisfying normalization, polarity coherence (factors through witness pair functor), and positivity. Natural substrate for Bayesian reasoning on Truth4.

registry_objects.title: Index Multiplication
registry_objects.summary: n * m = n + n + ... + n (m times): multiplication earned by structural recursion on addition.

registry_objects.title: Index Exponentiation
registry_objects.summary: n^m = n * n * ... * n (m times): exponentiation earned by structural recursion on multiplication.

registry_objects.title: Index Tetration
registry_objects.summary: n ^^m = n^(n^(...^n)) (m times): tetration earned by structural recursion on exponentiation. Terminal operation (ladder saturates here).

registry_objects.title: Program Monoid
registry_objects.summary: Programs = finite sequences of rho-instructions. Composition = sequential concatenation + normalization. Identity = empty program. The compositional substrate for future categories.

registry_objects.title: Three-Level Equality
registry_objects.summary: Three levels of sameness: (1) ontic identity (primitive), (2) address equivalence (decidable, NF-based), (3) shadow equality (external VM readout).

registry_objects.title: NF Address Encoding
registry_objects.summary: Every object x in Obj(tau) has a normal form X = ((A^^C)^B)*D via greedy peel-off of tetration, exponentiation, multiplication, and radial index.

registry_objects.title: Denotational Order
registry_objects.summary: The canonical linear order on Obj(tau): orbit-first (by K1 generator order), then depth-within-orbit. Extends K1 from generators to all objects.

registry_objects.title: ABCD Coordinate Chart
registry_objects.summary: Canonical coordinate chart Phi(x) = (A,B,C,D) via greedy peel-off; four typed coordinate functions (coord_pi, coord_gamma, coord_eta, coord_alpha).

registry_objects.title: Algebraic Lemniscate
registry_objects.summary: L defined as the bipolar spectral algebra H_tau = A_tau^(B) x A_tau^(C) with crossing point and polarity involution sigma. The algebraic pre-geometric definition of the lemniscate boundary. Geometric form S^1 v S^1 emerges in Book II. Earned from prime polarity, omega-germs, and split-complex discovery.

registry_objects.title: Boundary Ring and Scalars
registry_objects.summary: Primorial inverse limits; CRT factorization; boundary ring as structured scaffold for scalars. iota_tau = 2/(pi+e) as B/C dominance mediator (earned, not imposed).

registry_objects.title: Internal Divisibility
registry_objects.summary: a | b iff exists k in tau-Idx such that b = a * k. Decidable, reflexive, transitive. First relational concept earned from Part III arithmetic.

registry_objects.title: Internal Primes
registry_objects.summary: p is prime iff p >= 2 and only divisors are 1 and p. P_tau is the set of internal primes; infinite (Euclid's argument earned internally).

registry_objects.title: Tower Atom
registry_objects.summary: T(a,b,c) = (a^^c)^b for prime a, b >= 1, c >= 1. The nesting ((a^^c)^b) is forced by diagonal discipline; only binding from which all three parameters are uniquely recoverable.

registry_objects.title: Greedy Peel Algorithm
registry_objects.summary: Greedy peel-off: (1) find A = largest prime dividing X, (2) find C = maximal tetration height, (3) find B = maximal exponent, (4) D = remainder. Deterministic and terminating.

registry_objects.title: Prime Spectral Signature
registry_objects.summary: For prime p and bound N, sigma_N(p) = (B_N, C_N) records max exponent and max tetration height across objects with A = p up to N. Stabilizes asymptotically due to growth-rate separation.

registry_objects.title: Prime Enumeration and Sieve
registry_objects.summary: Prime enumeration nthPrime(k) = p_k, prime counting pi(n), and prime index (inverse). The earned Sieve of Eratosthenes: computed entirely from rho-folds via is_prime_bool. Semantic orbit projection from pi-orbit to alpha-orbit values.

registry_objects.title: Split-Complex Scalars
registry_objects.summary: Split-complex unit j with j^2 = +1 (not i^2 = -1). Earned from boundary ring structure. The foundational scalar field for tau-holomorphy.

registry_objects.title: Truth4 Logic
registry_objects.summary: T, F, B (both), N (neither) from polarity + stabilization. Explosion blocked structurally. Boolean logic = forgetful functor on Omega_tau.

registry_objects.title: Holomorphic Transformers
registry_objects.summary: KEY 3: omega-germ transformers as pre-categorical morphisms on the lemniscate boundary. HolFun, HolMap. Split-complex holomorphy gives tau full analytic structure.

registry_objects.title: Genealogical Decomposition (Spine)
registry_objects.summary: Iterate the canonical peel along the remainder D to produce a finite sequence of ABC-triplets. X is recoverable by multiplying the corresponding tower atoms. Spine Cayley length ell_spine(x) = number of triplets.

registry_objects.title: Address DAG
registry_objects.summary: Full quadtree (recurse on all 4 coordinates by index) globally deduplicated by index identity. Diamond-shaped finite DAG: branching out from root, reconverging via shared indices, terminating at alpha_1.

registry_objects.title: Omega-Tail (Compatible Tower)
registry_objects.summary: Compatible tower (x_k) on the primorial ladder M_k = prod of first k primes, with reduction maps. Pre-topological boundary data on bare-metal ontic elements. Polarity is a tail-stable predicate on omega-tails.

registry_objects.title: Polarized Omega-Germ
registry_objects.summary: B-polarized omega-germ: C-channel eventually constant while B-channel refines nontrivially. C-polarized: symmetric. Formalizes 'the B-channel wins' / 'the C-channel wins' as eventual stabilization of inverse system factors.

registry_objects.title: Bipolar Spectral Algebra
registry_objects.summary: H_tau = A_tau^(B) x A_tau^(C) with bipolar idempotents e_pm = (1 pm j)/2. Canonical decomposition of every element into B-sector and C-sector. Zero divisors managed by diagonal-free discipline.

registry_objects.title: Boundary Local Ring
registry_objects.summary: Ring structure on omega-tails from primorial inverse limit. CRT factors Z/M_k into B-prime and C-prime contributions. Earned ring operations on boundary data.

registry_objects.title: CRT Decomposition
registry_objects.summary: CRT decomposition and reconstruction on the primorial ladder: forward map x -> (x mod p_i), inverse map via coprime idempotents e_i, round-trip verified exhaustively by native_decide. Basis elements are idempotent, orthogonal, sum to unity. CRT coherence with primorial reduction verified.

registry_objects.title: Teichmueller Lift
registry_objects.summary: Canonical lift of single-prime residue r in Z/p_iZ to omega-tail via CRT reconstruction at each stage. Satisfies retraction (Lift_i(r) mod p_i = r), orthogonality (Lift_i(r) mod p_j = 0 for j != i), compatibility (compatible tower), multiplicativity, and decomposition (nat_to_tail = sum of lifts). All properties verified by native_decide.

registry_objects.title: tau-Membership Relation
registry_objects.summary: A in_tau B iff A | B (in the multiplicative structure on tau-Idx). Membership earned from divisibility; decidable, reflexive, antisymmetric. No ZFC axioms imported.

registry_objects.title: Set-Theoretic Operations
registry_objects.summary: Union = lcm, intersection = gcd, difference via prime factorization stripping. Set operations earned from the multiplicative structure on tau-Idx.

registry_objects.title: Bounded Powerset
registry_objects.summary: P_tau(X) = set of all divisors of X. Always finite: |P_tau(X)| = product of (e_i + 1) over prime factorization. No Russell paradox: strict divisibility decreases value.

registry_objects.title: Master Constant iota_tau
registry_objects.summary: iota_tau = 2/(pi+e) ~ 0.341304. The asymptotic B/C dominance mediator: parametrizes the split-complex decomposition and measures the asymmetry between the two lemniscate lobes. Earned from prime distribution, not imposed.

registry_objects.title: Number Tower
registry_objects.summary: N_tau subset Z_tau subset Q_tau subset R_tau subset C_tau. Integers via Grothendieck group, rationals via field of fractions, reals via Cauchy completion, complexes via R_tau[i].

registry_objects.title: Constructive Reals
registry_objects.summary: R_tau: Cauchy completion of Q_tau with explicit modulus of convergence. Constructive reals aligned with computable/effectively presented analysis.

registry_objects.title: Lemniscate Characters
registry_objects.summary: Characters chi: L -> Z_hat_tau[j] as ring homomorphisms from the bipolar spectral algebra to split-complex scalars. Fundamental characters chi_+ and chi_- project onto B-sector and C-sector.

registry_objects.title: Character Group
registry_objects.summary: The set of all characters on L with pointwise multiplication. Every character traces back to the bipolar partition of primes.

registry_objects.title: Crossing Point
registry_objects.summary: Where the two lobes of L meet (algebraic version). The crossing point is where B-sector and C-sector intersect; not a smooth point. Geometric S^1 v S^1 emerges in Book II.

registry_objects.title: Bipolar Fourier Transform
registry_objects.summary: Formal transform on L using the character group. Expresses functions on L as sums over characters. Feeds into the Central Theorem: O(tau^3) = A_spec(L).

registry_objects.title: Subobject Classifier Preview
registry_objects.summary: Preview of Omega_tau: Truth4 will serve as the subobject classifier in the earned topos (Part XIII). The four truth values give tau's internal logic its paraconsistent character.

registry_objects.title: D-Differentiability
registry_objects.summary: A function f: H_tau -> H_tau is D-differentiable if in sector coordinates (u,v) = (a+b, a-b), it decomposes as f(u,v) = (g(u), h(v)). Formalized as SectorFun: a pair (g, h) of sector component maps.

registry_objects.title: Split-CR Equations
registry_objects.summary: The split-complex Cauchy-Riemann equations: dU/da = dV/db and dU/db = dV/da. In sector coordinates: dF+/dv = 0 and dF-/du = 0. Formalized as has_split_cr_form predicate.

registry_objects.title: Omega-Germ Transformer
registry_objects.summary: An omega-germ transformer maps omega-tails to sector-pair values. Carries both a SectorFun (D-holomorphic structure) and a StageFun (stagewise evaluation for tower coherence).

registry_objects.title: Tower Coherence
registry_objects.summary: Tower coherence: reduce(f(n, l), k) = f(n, k) for k <= l. A naturality condition on the primorial inverse system: reducing the output first, or reducing the input first and then applying, gives the same result.

registry_objects.title: Tau-Holomorphic Function
registry_objects.summary: A tau-holomorphic function (HolFun) = D-holomorphic + tower-coherent germ transformer. The D-holomorphic condition is structural (SectorFun); tower coherence is the additional rigidity constraint.

registry_objects.title: Tau-Holomorphic Map
registry_objects.summary: A tau-holomorphic map bundles a HolFun with source and target object indices in tau-Idx. Provides the morphism data for the earned category Cat_tau (Part XIII).

registry_objects.title: Hol(L)
registry_objects.summary: Hol(L): the space of all tau-holomorphic functions on the algebraic lemniscate. By the Identity Theorem, elements are uniquely determined by their values at any single primorial depth.

registry_objects.title: Tau-Arrow
registry_objects.summary: A tau-arrow from source to target is a HolFun (tau-holomorphic function). Two arrows are equal iff their underlying HolFuns agree extensionally at all inputs and stages.

registry_objects.title: Cat_tau
registry_objects.summary: Cat_tau: the earned category with objects = TauIdx, morphisms = tau-arrows. Identity from id_holfun, composition from HolFun composition, associativity from Part XII. Not imported but EARNED from the monoid structure.

registry_objects.title: Tau-Functor
registry_objects.summary: A tau-functor maps objects to objects. In thin Cat_tau, functors are determined by their object map alone (at most one morphism between any pair, so the morphism map is uniquely determined).

registry_objects.title: Natural Transformation
registry_objects.summary: A natural transformation between tau-functors. In a thin category, naturality is AUTOMATIC: the naturality square commutes because there is at most one arrow in each direction.

registry_objects.title: Yoneda Embedding
registry_objects.summary: The Yoneda embedding y: Cat_tau -> PSh(Cat_tau) sends X to Hom(-, X). In thin Cat_tau, representable presheaves are subterminal (all hom-sets are singletons).

registry_objects.title: Finite Limits in Cat_tau
registry_objects.summary: Cat_tau has all finite limits: terminal object (index 1), products via Cantor pairing, equalizers (trivial in thin category — identity or empty), pullbacks from products + equalizers.

registry_objects.title: Tau-Site
registry_objects.summary: The tau-site: Cat_tau equipped with primorial coverage. At each depth k, the covering family for object X consists of the CRT residues mod primes p_1, ..., p_k. Encodes arithmetic structure categorically.

registry_objects.title: Presheaf Topos
registry_objects.summary: PSh(Cat_tau): the presheaf topos. A presheaf assigns to each object a set (modeled as a predicate). Includes terminal/initial presheaves and pointwise product/coproduct operations.

registry_objects.title: Characteristic Morphism
registry_objects.summary: The characteristic morphism chi_S: X -> Omega_tau assigns a Truth4 value based on B-sector and C-sector membership. T = both confirm, F = both deny, B = overdetermined, N = underdetermined. Pullback of true along chi recovers the subobject.

registry_objects.title: Earned Topos
registry_objects.summary: The earned topos E_tau = PSh(Cat_tau) with Omega_tau as subobject classifier. Bundles the Grothendieck topos structure with the four-valued classifier and truth arrow.

registry_objects.title: Categorical Product
registry_objects.summary: The categorical product of two presheaves: pointwise conjunction of support predicates. P x Q maps each object X to P(X) AND Q(X). Projections extract each factor.

registry_objects.title: Cartesian Monoidal Structure
registry_objects.summary: The cartesian monoidal structure (E_tau, x, 1): unit is the terminal presheaf (all-true), tensor is pointwise conjunction. Left and right unit laws hold.

registry_objects.title: Categorical Coproduct
registry_objects.summary: The categorical coproduct (wedge product) of two presheaves: pointwise disjunction. P v Q maps each object X to P(X) OR Q(X). Injections embed each factor.

registry_objects.title: Bi-Monoidal Structure
registry_objects.summary: The bi-monoidal structure on E_tau: product (x) and coproduct (v) with distributivity. Multiplicative unit = terminal presheaf, additive unit = initial presheaf. Absorption: P x 0 = 0.

registry_objects.title: Internal Hom
registry_objects.summary: The internal hom Q^P: pointwise Boolean implication. (Q^P)(X) = true iff P(X) implies Q(X). This gives exponentials in E_tau.

registry_objects.title: Spectral Coefficients
registry_objects.summary: Spectral coefficients of a StageFun at input n, stage k: the B-sector and C-sector outputs. Together they fully determine the function value.

registry_objects.title: Restriction Map
registry_objects.summary: The restriction map: restrict a StageFun to inputs NOT in a given subset K. Returns 0 for deleted inputs. Agrees with original outside K.

registry_objects.title: Primorial Thinness
registry_objects.summary: A subset K is primordially thin at stage k if it occupies fewer than k-1 of the first k CRT positions (leaving >= 2 free directions). The tau-analog of codimension >= 2. Empty set is globally thin.

registry_objects.title: Earned Stage-Determined Point
registry_objects.summary: An earned interior point: a value obtained by extending boundary data via Hartogs extension. Carries a tower-coherent StageFun and produces interior values that are self-consistent (reduced).

registry_objects.title: Generative Counting Principle
registry_objects.summary: Counting as a structural feature of tau: every tau-set is generated by rho-iteration from seeds, inheriting countability from the orbit structure. No set outruns the generative act.

registry_objects.title: Omega-Germ Approach
registry_objects.summary: Omega-germs as approaches to infinity: compatible towers on the primorial ladder encode how a sequence approaches omega. Replaces the cardinality hierarchy with a single structural concept of asymptotic approach.

registry_objects.title: Meta-Logical Substrate
registry_objects.summary: The meta-logical substrate: the collection of CIC structural rules, type-formation principles, and axioms provided by the proof assistant that are not derived from K0-K6. Classifies contraction, weakening, and exchange by their object-level status under K5.

registry_objects.title: Diagonal-Linear Correspondence
registry_objects.summary: Structural isomorphism between K5's diagonal discipline and the !-free fragment of Girard's linear logic: no unearned diagonals = no free contraction, channel consumption = linear resource tracking, saturation = finite resource budget.

registry_objects.title: Program Monoid as Linear Calculus
registry_objects.summary: Reinterpretation of the program monoid (I.D14) as a linear sequent calculus: programs = linear proofs, concatenation = cut rule, NF-Confluence (I.L02) = cut-elimination, four orbit channels = linear context zones.

registry_objects.title: Self-Hosting Degree Classification
registry_objects.summary: Four levels: none, partial, fragment, full. Classifies proof-theoretic self-hosting by internalization depth.

registry_objects.title: CCC-Linear Dichotomy
registry_objects.summary: CCC side has free diagonals, Lawvere barrier. Star-autonomous side has no free diagonals, no barrier.

registry_objects.title: Enrichment Frontier Classification
registry_objects.summary: Three statuses: achieved (E0-E1), partially achieved (E1-E2), unprecedented (E2-E3).

registry_objects.title: Primorial Presheaf
registry_objects.summary: The primorial presheaf F : Prim^op -> Ring sends d to Z/M_dZ with reduction maps. Its split-complex extension F_j sends d to Z/M_dZ[j]. The spectral presheaf pair (F_B, F_C) is the sector decomposition.

registry_objects.title: Constructive Reals
registry_objects.summary: TauReal: constructive reals via Cauchy completion of TauRat. Represented as sequences of TauRat approximations with pointwise equivalence. Every TauReal is explicitly specified by a constructive sequence.

registry_objects.title: Elliptic Complex Field
registry_objects.summary: TauComplex = TauReal[i]/(i^2+1): the elliptic complex field. Pairs (re, im) of TauReal values with multiplication (ac-bd, ad+bc). The imaginary unit i satisfies i^2 = -1.

registry_objects.title: Elliptic-Hyperbolic Dichotomy
registry_objects.summary: The elliptic-hyperbolic dichotomy: TauComplex (i^2=-1, field, no zero divisors) versus SplitComplex (j^2=+1, ring, zero divisors). Both are algebraically earned; they coexist as complementary structures within tau.

registry_objects.title: Elliptic Quaternions
registry_objects.summary: TauQuaternion = TauReal-algebra {1,i,j,k} with Hamilton product: i^2=j^2=k^2=ijk=-1. Non-commutativity is earned as a structural consequence of extending beyond two dimensions.

registry_objects.title: Cyclotomic Fields
registry_objects.summary: Cyclotomic fields: roots of unity z^n = 1 mod m, primitive roots, and their connection to CRT decomposition. The Galois group Gal(Q(zeta_n)/Q) is isomorphic to (Z/nZ)^times.

registry_objects.title: Diagonal Resonance
registry_objects.summary: Diagonal resonance: the interaction resonance between three individually benign components — (L) meta-level contraction/free token reuse, (E) equality-as-congruence with full substitution, (P) ontic self-products with diagonal materialization — that jointly produce identity pathology in foundations.

registry_objects.title: Identity Slippage
registry_objects.summary: Identity slippage: the partial decoherence of ontic self-identity where distinct ontic objects cannot be preserved as distinct under any global projection into a VM exhibiting diagonal resonance. The boundary between identity-of-reference and equality-as-relation is smeared.

registry_objects.title: Shadow Identity
registry_objects.summary: Shadow identity: an implicit identification channel — equivalence witness, congruence step, or substitution bridge — that behaves operationally like a morphism of sameness without being ontically constructed. The operational consequence of diagonal resonance.

registry_objects.title: Identity-Faithful Reception
registry_objects.summary: Identity-faithful reception: a VM system S can receive tau ontically only if there exists an interpretation functor P: C_tau -> C_S that is faithful on identity — reflects equality/isomorphism back to tau-identity, preserves identity morphisms, and maps distinct tau-objects to distinct S-objects.

registry_objects.title: Structural Instability
registry_objects.summary: Structural instability: a foundation exhibits structural instability if diagonal resonance prevents the existence of a canonical, identity-faithful intended semantics — the system cannot internally stabilize a unique ontic closure (omega) and cannot fix ontology/reference without VM-relativity.

registry_objects.title: Orbit-Set Map
registry_objects.summary: Orbit-Set Map: assigns to every tau-element a structurally determined set via five families. Set(alpha_n) = {alpha_k : k | n} (divisor set = tau-membership); Set(pi_n) = first n primes; Set(gamma_n) = vertical prime tower; Set(eta_n) = horizontal prime sweep; Set(omega) = O_alpha union {omega}. The alpha-orbit case is exactly tau-membership (I.D31). All set-elements from O_alpha only (plus omega in Set(omega)).

registry_objects.title: τ-Measure Space
registry_objects.summary: Constructive measure space on the primorial tower. At each stage k, Z/M_k Z carries the normalized counting measure μ_k(S) = |S|/M_k. The τ-measure space is the projective family of stages with compatible counting measures.

registry_objects.title: Tower σ-Algebra
registry_objects.summary: Tower-measurable sets: compatible families of predicates S_k on Z/M_k Z such that preimage under reduction preserves membership. At finite stage, every subset is measurable (full power set σ-algebra).

registry_objects.title: Galois Automorphism
registry_objects.summary: A Galois automorphism at stage k: multiplication by a unit a with gcd(a, M_k)=1. Preserves ring structure: σ_a(x+y) = σ_a(x)+σ_a(y), σ_a(xy) = σ_a(x)·σ_a(y).

registry_objects.title: Galois Group of Primorial Stage
registry_objects.summary: The Galois group at stage k is (Z/M_k Z)×, the group of units. Its order is φ(M_k) = ∏(p_i - 1) for primes p_i ≤ p_k. Verified: φ(2)=1, φ(6)=2, φ(30)=8.

registry_objects.title: τ-Integral
registry_objects.summary: The τ-integral of f at stage k: ∫_k f = (Σ f(x)) / M_k. Expectation under the counting measure μ_k on Z/M_k Z.

registry_objects.title: Universe Postulate
registry_objects.summary: Postulates the existence of the totality tau as a universe of discourse. Implicit in Lean type system (Generator : Type, TauObj : Type). Distinguishes tau (ambient type) from omega (fixed-point element within tau).

registry_objects.title: Strict Order (K1)
registry_objects.summary: alpha < pi < gamma < eta < omega is a strict total order on the 5 generators.

registry_objects.title: Omega Fixed Point (K2)
registry_objects.summary: rho(omega) = omega; omega absorbs all operations.

registry_objects.title: Orbit-Seeded Generation (K3)
registry_objects.summary: Each generator g in {alpha, pi, gamma, eta} seeds its orbit ray O_g = {rho^n(g) : n >= 0}.

registry_objects.title: No-Jump / Cover (K4)
registry_objects.summary: rho is a successor within each orbit (no skipping); covers are primitive.

registry_objects.title: Beacon Non-Successor (K5)
registry_objects.summary: omega is NOT in the image of rho restricted to any orbit ray; omega is unreachable by finite iteration.

registry_objects.title: Object Closure (K6)
registry_objects.summary: Obj(tau) = {omega} union O_alpha union O_pi union O_gamma union O_eta; no other objects exist.

registry_objects.title: Pentation Non-Injectivity
registry_objects.summary: No fifth orbit channel exists (K6), so pentation cannot be equipped with canonical injectivity within tau.

registry_objects.title: NF-Confluence
registry_objects.summary: Normalization of programs is confluent: any two reduction paths yield the same normal form. Proved via termination + local confluence + Newman's Lemma.

registry_objects.title: No-Tie Determinism
registry_objects.summary: Maximal tetration height C is uniquely determined. Tower atoms T(A,b1,c1) = T(A,b2,c2) implies (b1,c1) = (b2,c2). Super-exponential growth of tetration prevents ties.

registry_objects.title: Strict Remainder Descent
registry_objects.summary: D < X whenever X >= 2. Tower atom >= 2, so remainder D <= X/2 < X. Prime-stratum descent: largest prime of D is strictly less than A.

registry_objects.title: Growth Escape
registry_objects.summary: Tetration escapes the primorial tower: for any tower depth d, there exists c such that 2^^c mod M_d != 2^^c. Quantitative shadow of saturation — the 4th hyperoperation level produces values that outrun any finite primorial approximation.

registry_objects.title: Well-Foundedness of Membership
registry_objects.summary: No infinite descending in_tau-chains: if A_1 in_tau A_2 in_tau ... with strict containment, the chain terminates (divisibility is well-founded above 1).

registry_objects.title: Tail Agreement Propagation
registry_objects.summary: If two tower-coherent stagewise functions agree at stage d0 for all inputs, they agree at ALL stages k <= d0. The downward direction: agreement at a fine stage implies agreement at all coarser stages.

registry_objects.title: CRT Extension
registry_objects.summary: CRT Extension: tower coherence constrains function output via the reduce map. For tower-coherent f: reduce(f.b_fun(n,l), k) = f.b_fun(n,k) for k <= l. Output at any stage is already reduced.

registry_objects.title: Generator Distinctness
registry_objects.summary: All five generators are pairwise distinct (immediate from K1 strict order).

registry_objects.title: rho Injectivity Per Orbit
registry_objects.summary: rho is injective on each orbit ray (from K4 no-jump/cover property).

registry_objects.title: Pairwise Disjointness of Orbits
registry_objects.summary: The five sets {omega}, O_alpha, O_pi, O_gamma, O_eta are pairwise disjoint.

registry_objects.title: Orbit Countability
registry_objects.summary: Each orbit ray O_g is countably infinite (isomorphic to N as a totally ordered set).

registry_objects.title: Tetration Injectivity
registry_objects.summary: Tetration is injective on the canonical domain: distinct inputs yield distinct towers.

registry_objects.title: Arithmetic Laws
registry_objects.summary: tau-Idx with index addition and multiplication forms a commutative semiring: commutativity, associativity, distributivity, identity elements.

registry_objects.title: Well-Ordering of Obj(tau)
registry_objects.summary: (Obj(tau), <_tau) is a well-ordering of order type omega*4+1: four copies of omega (one per orbit ray) followed by the beacon omega.

registry_objects.title: Dimension Theorem (dim_tau = 4)
registry_objects.summary: dim_tau = 4: the four ABCD coordinates are pairwise independent (sufficiency) and no three suffice (necessity). Dimension is earned from arithmetic hierarchy, not postulated.

registry_objects.title: Metric Inequality
registry_objects.summary: ell_spine(x) <= ell_DAG(x) <= ell_occ(x). Three canonical complexity metrics: spine length (radial depth), DAG size (memoized work), occurrence size (naive work).

registry_objects.title: Membership Decidability
registry_objects.summary: The tau-membership relation is decidable: given A, B in tau-Idx, we can computably determine whether A in_tau B.

registry_objects.title: Distributive Lattice
registry_objects.summary: (tau-Idx, in_tau) forms a distributive lattice under gcd (meet) and lcm (join). Distributivity follows from the FTA.

registry_objects.title: Countability of Set(tau)
registry_objects.summary: |Set(tau)| = aleph_0. All tau-sets are countable. No Cantor diagonal, no uncountable sets, no non-measurable sets. Everything constructive.

registry_objects.title: Boolean Recovery
registry_objects.summary: Boolean logic as a quotient of Truth4: collapsing B and N recovers classical two-valued logic. The forgetful map Truth4 -> Bool is a lattice homomorphism.

registry_objects.title: Omega Unique Fixed Seed
registry_objects.summary: rho(x) = x iff seed(x) = omega. Omega is the unique fixed seed of rho among ALL objects (not just generators). Non-omega seeds always advance depth by 1.

registry_objects.title: Sum Zero Iff Both Zero
registry_objects.summary: n + m = 0 iff n = 0 and m = 0. Contrapositive: if either summand is positive, the sum is positive.

registry_objects.title: Positive Core Closure
registry_objects.summary: N+ = {n > 0} is closed under add, mul, exp; successor is always positive. Arithmetic never falls into zero unless it starts there.

registry_objects.title: Universal Additive Cancellation
registry_objects.summary: n + a = n + b implies a = b. Additive cancellation is UNIVERSAL: no positivity guard needed. Follows from rho-injectivity.

registry_objects.title: Zero Vacuous
registry_objects.summary: Zero is vacuous: (1) not prime, (2) not a successor, (3) divisible by everything, (4) unique multiplicative absorber. A non-participant rather than a destructive element.

registry_objects.title: Integral Domain
registry_objects.summary: n * m = 0 iff n = 0 or m = 0. tau-Idx has no zero divisors (integral domain property). Forward direction uses positive core closure.

registry_objects.title: Ultra Dist Self
registry_objects.summary: d(t, t) = 0 for every omega-tail t. Identity of indiscernibles for the primorial divergence depth.

registry_objects.title: Congruent Tails Agree
registry_objects.summary: n = m (mod M_k) implies canonical tails agree at level k. Agreement at each primorial level is a finite modular check. Underlies Cauchy-compactness of the profinite completion.

registry_objects.title: Sector Independence
registry_objects.summary: Every SectorFun is sector-independent by construction: B-output depends only on B-input, C-output depends only on C-input. The structural content of the split-CR equations.

registry_objects.title: No Simultaneous Projection
registry_objects.summary: No Simultaneous Projection: the diagonal-free discipline prevents any omega-tail from projecting nontrivially onto BOTH idempotent sectors e_plus and e_minus simultaneously.

registry_objects.title: HolFun Associativity
registry_objects.summary: HolFun composition is associative: (f1 o f2) o f3 = f1 o (f2 o f3). Follows from function extensionality. Together with identity and composition closure, HolFun forms a monoid.

registry_objects.title: Thin Category
registry_objects.summary: Cat_tau is thin: between any two objects there is at most one morphism. Direct corollary of the tau-Identity Theorem — if two tower-coherent functions agree at any depth, they agree everywhere.

registry_objects.title: Countable Topos
registry_objects.summary: PSh(Cat_tau) is a countable topos: Cat_tau has countable objects and at most one morphism between each pair (thin). Presheaves are countably generated by functions TauIdx -> Bool.

registry_objects.title: Paraconsistent Character
registry_objects.summary: The earned topos E_tau has a Boolean lattice (Omega_tau = 2x2, complement law holds) but paraconsistent material implication (B => F = N != T, explosion fails). The subobject complement law fails: elements with chi_S in {B, N} belong to neither S nor S^c. Boolean lattice coexists with paraconsistent implication — a structural consequence of the two spectral sectors.

registry_objects.title: Self-Enrichment
registry_objects.summary: E_tau is self-enriched: internal hom gives an internal presheaf of morphisms. Every internal hom Q^P is itself a Presheaf.

registry_objects.title: Passage to Book II
registry_objects.summary: Passage to Book II: the canonical export structure. Book I delivers Cat_tau, the earned topos E_tau, the holomorphic function space Hol(L), the Identity Theorem, and the four-valued subobject classifier. Book II will use these to prove O(tau^3) = A_spec(L).

registry_objects.title: Counting as Structural Feature
registry_objects.summary: Countability is not a limitation but a structural feature: every tau-object is reachable by finite rho-iteration, so every tau-set is at most countable by construction.

registry_objects.title: No Unearned Decimal Diagonal
registry_objects.summary: No unearned decimal diagonal: tau-reals are constructive Cauchy sequences with explicit moduli. The diagonal construction requires non-constructive choice over uncountably many positions, which tau does not provide.

registry_objects.title: No Unrestricted Comprehension
registry_objects.summary: No unrestricted comprehension: tau-sets are bounded powersets (divisor sets), not arbitrary collections. The set {x : x divides n} is always finite, blocking Russell-type diagonal constructions.

registry_objects.title: No Free Cartesian Diagonal
registry_objects.summary: No free Cartesian diagonal: the diagonal discipline (I.D03) prevents free contraction/reuse, blocking the Cartesian product diagonal map that Cantor's argument requires.

registry_objects.title: Ultrametric Replaces Cardinality
registry_objects.summary: The ultrametric structure on omega-germs (primorial divergence depth) replaces the cardinality hierarchy. Size distinctions between infinite sets are replaced by depth-of-agreement distinctions between omega-germs.

registry_objects.title: Classical.em Eliminability
registry_objects.summary: Both uses of Classical.em in TauLib (Coordinates/Primes.lean lines 110, 172) are applied to decidable predicates (divisibility of natural numbers) and can be replaced by decidable case analysis without changing any theorem statement.

registry_objects.title: TauReal Ring Axioms
registry_objects.summary: TauReal satisfies all commutative ring axioms up to equivalence: commutativity, associativity, identities, inverses, and distributivity. Each axiom reduces to the corresponding TauRat axiom applied pointwise.

registry_objects.title: Extensionality
registry_objects.summary: Extensionality of the orbit-set map: the map Set is injective on each orbit and globally. Distinct tau-elements represent distinct sets. Alpha-orbit injectivity via unique maximum alpha_n; pi-orbit via cardinality; gamma/eta via structural signatures.

registry_objects.title: Self-Containment Partition
registry_objects.summary: Self-Containment Partition: X in Set(X) iff X in O_alpha union {omega}. The alpha-orbit and omega are 'opaque' (self-containing); the solenoidal orbits O_pi, O_gamma, O_eta are 'transparent' (non-self-containing organizing principles). Third position between ZFC (never reflexive) and divisibility (always reflexive).

registry_objects.title: Order Bound
registry_objects.summary: Order Bound: for all A in Set(alpha_n), A <= alpha_n in the internal order on tau-Idx. alpha_n is the maximum of Set(alpha_n). Membership 'looks downward' from the representing element.

registry_objects.title: Measure Compatibility
registry_objects.summary: The projective family of counting measures is compatible: for any tower-measurable set, the measure at stage k+1 (projected down) equals the measure at stage k. μ_{k+1}(π⁻¹(S_k)) = μ_k(S_k).

registry_objects.title: CRT-Galois Decomposition
registry_objects.summary: The Galois group decomposes via CRT: Gal_k ≅ ∏(Z/p_i Z)× for i=1..k. Order equality φ(M_k) = ∏(p_i-1) verified computationally at stages 1-3.

registry_objects.title: Monotone Convergence
registry_objects.summary: For tower-compatible monotone function families, the sequence of integrals is non-decreasing across stages.

registry_objects.title: No Second Linearity
registry_objects.summary: The ABCD chart Phi is not linear: Phi(X+Y) != Phi(X)+Phi(Y) for alpha-ray addition. NF encoding interleaves multiplicative and exponential data, destroying additivity. Concrete counterexample: X=2, Y=4.

registry_objects.title: Bayesian Factorization
registry_objects.summary: Every tau-Bayesian state factors: S = S_+ o e_+ + S_- o e_-, where S_+/S_- are classical probability distributions on {T,F}. Boolean recovery applies to each sector independently.

registry_objects.title: Axiom Independence
registry_objects.summary: Six countermodel sketches showing K1-K6 are mutually independent: no proper subset entails the remaining axiom.

registry_objects.title: Structural Rules Inventory
registry_objects.summary: Inventory of CIC features used by TauLib: inductive types (essential), dependent types (essential), pattern matching (essential), universe polymorphism (cosmetic), Classical.em (2 of 77 modules, eliminable). 74/77 modules fully constructive.

registry_objects.title: Linear Logic Glossary
registry_objects.summary: Reference glossary of Girard's linear logic (1987): multiplicative connectives (tensor, par), additive connectives (with, plus), exponential modalities (! of-course, ? why-not), linear negation. Without ! and ?, every proposition is used exactly once.

registry_objects.title: Gap Declaration
registry_objects.summary: Gap declaration: what remains unearned at the end of Book I — CIC type formation rules, CIC structural rules at the meta-level, funext/propext as kernel axioms. These are starting conditions, not defects. Book III's enrichment ladder (E0->E1->E2->E3) will progressively internalize the proof theory.

registry_objects.title: Proof-Theoretic Landscape Survey
registry_objects.summary: Tabular survey of 11 approaches to self-hosting: ZFC, PA, Willard, Feferman, Girard, Altenkirch-Kaposi, Bocquet-Kaposi-Sattler, Joyal, Moerdijk-Palmgren, 2LTT, HoTT, tau.

registry_objects.title: Barr's Star-Autonomous Categories
registry_objects.summary: Barr 1979: symmetric monoidal closed with dualizing object. Tensor not cartesian, no general diagonal. Models multiplicative linear logic.

registry_objects.title: E0-E3 Literature Map
registry_objects.summary: Tabular mapping of each E-transition to closest precedent, gap, and tau feature.

registry_objects.title: Scale Declaration
registry_objects.summary: Book III's E2-E3 transition is unprecedented at meaningful strength. Architecture is positioned to attempt it, not guaranteed to achieve it.

registry_objects.title: Hurwitz Classification Preview
registry_objects.summary: Hurwitz classification preview: exactly four normed division algebras over the reals (R, C, H, O). Tau earns three of them: TauReal, TauComplex, TauQuaternion. Octonions require Book II's topological structure.

registry_objects.title: Galois Theory Preview
registry_objects.summary: Galois theory preview: the cyclotomic Galois group (Z/nZ)^times acts on roots of unity by exponentiation. This algebraic infrastructure serves as the bridge to Book II's topological Galois theory and to the Langlands connection in Book III.

registry_objects.title: Five Reasons Why The Bug Hides
registry_objects.summary: Five reasons diagonal resonance is uniquely hard to detect: (a) not a bug in one module, (b) produces slippage not a crash, (c) everywhere and nowhere, (d) hides behind utility, (e) only visible from unique closure demand.

registry_objects.title: Orthodox Foundations Under the Lens
registry_objects.summary: Examination of three orthodox foundations under the diagonal resonance lens: ZFC (free contraction in FOL, extensional equality, Cartesian products), CIC/Lean (lambda contraction, definitional equality, Sigma-types), HoTT (structural rules in meta-theory, rich path identity, products). Each exhibits diagonal resonance at different levels.

registry_objects.title: Implications for Absolute Meaning
registry_objects.summary: Implications for absolute meaning: the infinity zoo (aleph_0, aleph_1, aleph_omega, ...) is a symptom of identity slippage, not a feature. Absolute meaning requires an omega-like rigid anchor. Diagonal-resonant kernels cannot host it canonically.

registry_objects.title: Honest Scope Declaration
registry_objects.summary: Honest scope declaration: the structural instability diagnosis is not a claim that orthodox mathematics is wrong. It explains WHY non-canonicity, model-relativity, and the infinity zoo arise, and WHY tau avoids them. The cost: no epsilon-delta, no local smoothness, no classical Laplacian without earning them in Books II-III.

registry_objects.title: Inseparability of N and omega
registry_objects.summary: Inseparability of N and omega: O_alpha (the positive naturals) is NOT a valid tau-internal set. No X in tau has Set(X) = O_alpha. The closest is Set(omega) = O_alpha union {omega} = N^+ union {infinity}. The counting scaffold and its closure point are inseparable — the set-theoretic expression of earned infinity.

registry_objects.title: Finite-Infinite Boundary
registry_objects.summary: Finite-Infinite Boundary: radial orbits (alpha, pi) yield finite sets; solenoidal orbits (gamma, eta) yield infinite sets; omega yields the universal set. The finite-infinite transition coincides with the radial-solenoidal boundary — the set-theoretic signature of the structural divide between counting infrastructure and power infrastructure.

registry_objects.title: Duality and Atoms
registry_objects.summary: Vertical-Horizontal Duality and Set-Theoretic Atoms: gamma explores depth (one prime, all powers), eta explores breadth (all primes, one power), mirroring the fiber-base decomposition. Set(eta_1) = canonical prime set. For any prime p, Set(alpha_p) = {alpha_1, alpha_p} — primes are set-theoretic atoms whose only divisors are 1 and themselves.

registry_objects.title: Wiring Primitives
registry_objects.summary: Five elementary wiring primitives (Identity, Swap, Fold, Merge, Lift) are the building blocks from which all programs are assembled. The diagonal discipline constrains Lift to three levels.

registry_objects.title: Product-Free Operator Definitions
registry_objects.summary: Route B axiomatizes arithmetic operations directly as finite-support rewrite functors on single channels, without defining them as iterations. Product-free: no Cartesian product needed. Both routes yield the same category.

registry_objects.title: Route B Axioms Comparison
registry_objects.summary: Route B uses 13 axioms K0'-K12' (vs Route A's 7 axioms K0-K6). K7'-K9' axiomatize rewrite functors; K12' asserts saturation. Route A chosen for tighter foundation; Route B validates uniqueness.

registry_objects.title: Normalization Endofunctors M and E
registry_objects.summary: Route B defines M (multiplicative) and E (exponential) normalization endofunctors on Supp, with M∘E=M. In Route A, these are derived from the diagonal discipline. Existence in both routes confirms robustness.

registry_objects.title: Address Combinators: Merge and Lift
registry_objects.summary: Merge combines programs on disjoint channels; Lift promotes from one level to the next. Program-monoid realizations of the wiring primitives (Ch 5), reducing to fold-chain operations via NF-Confluence.

registry_objects.title: CGANF to ABCD Design Evolution
registry_objects.summary: The 1st Edition term CGANF replaced by ABCD coordinate chart in 2nd Edition. Purely terminological; underlying mathematics (greedy peel, tower atoms, unique factorization) identical. ABCD aligns with fibration preview.

registry_objects.title: Cluster Collapse in ABCD Context
registry_objects.summary: 1st Edition cluster collapse is automatic in ABCD: greedy peel extracts dominant tower atom (A,B,C), remainder D absorbs all cluster structure in one pass. No separate collapse step needed.

registry_objects.title: Token-Set vs Tuple Encoding
registry_objects.summary: ABCD chart is extensional (tuple); alternative token-set encoding is intensional (construction process). Hyperfactorization Theorem guarantees both agree. Token-set perspective appears in Lean formalization.

registry_objects.title: Dimension Readout Functors
registry_objects.summary: Four canonical readout functors project from Obj(tau) to individual coordinate ranges. Base readouts (D,A) and fiber readouts (B,C) decompose via the fibration preview. Catalog items in Appendix registry.

registry_objects.title: Pairing Density
registry_objects.summary: B-dominant and C-dominant primes interleave: every B-dominant prime has infinitely many C-dominant partners within bounded gap. Connected to two-lobe lemniscate structure.

registry_objects.title: PolStream Aperiodicity
registry_objects.summary: PolStream has no eventual period: periodicity would contradict either infinitude of both polarity classes or crossing-point uniqueness.

registry_objects.title: Lemniscate Lipschitz Forward Reference
registry_objects.summary: Lipschitz descent analysis of lemniscate dynamics requires Book II analytic tools (holomorphic decay estimates, boundary regularity). Forward reference.

registry_objects.title: Quaternion Open Question
registry_objects.summary: Open question: Can the split-complex extension be iterated via Cayley-Dickson doubling? Crossing-point uniqueness suggests NO (second doubling would require two crossing points). Full proof requires Book II torus degeneration.

registry_objects.title: Lean Bayesian Status
registry_objects.summary: Boolean fragment formalized in TauLib.Logic.BooleanRecovery. Bayesian extension (tau-Bayesian states, factorization, witness pair functor) is research program, not yet in Lean.

registry_objects.title: Distributivity from Combinators
registry_objects.summary: Distributivity theorem I.T27 re-read as Merge/Fold interchange law: the program-monoid shadow of a(b+c) = ab + ac. Combinator perspective useful for Book III spectral forces as bi-monoidal natural transformations.

registry_objects.title: Ontic Closure
registry_objects.summary: Obj(tau) = {omega} union O_alpha union O_pi union O_gamma union O_eta, and this set is ontically sealed -- no further objects can be created.

registry_objects.title: Iterator Ladder Saturation
registry_objects.summary: The iterator ladder has exactly 4 levels (0-3); higher hyper-operations lose canonical injectivity because K6 prevents a 5th orbit channel.

registry_objects.title: Composition Associativity
registry_objects.summary: Program composition is associative. A THEOREM, not an axiom: proved via normalization confluence (NF-Confluence Theorem).

registry_objects.title: Hyperfactorization Theorem
registry_objects.summary: HINGE THEOREM 1: Every x in Obj(tau) has a unique canonical NF via three critical lemmas (tetration injectivity, no-tie determinism, strict remainder descent). Provable in ZFC.

registry_objects.title: Prime Polarity Theorem
registry_objects.summary: HINGE THEOREM 2: Primes carry canonical bipolar polarization via gamma/eta dominance -- global spectrum with finite (local) witnesses. Provable in ZFC.

registry_objects.title: Global Hartogs
registry_objects.summary: Boundary determines interior: interior points earned without coordinates via holomorphic continuation. Book I climax and canonical passage to Book II.

registry_objects.title: Rigidity of tau
registry_objects.summary: Aut(tau) = {id}. Every automorphism fixes all generators (named constants) and all orbit elements (by induction on depth).

registry_objects.title: Categoricity of tau_0
registry_objects.summary: tau_0 is categorical: any two models are uniquely isomorphic. The unique isomorphism maps rho^n(g) to (rho^M)^n(g^M).

registry_objects.title: FTA on tau-Idx
registry_objects.summary: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic on tau-Idx: every n >= 2 has a unique prime factorization. Proved via strong induction (existence) and Euclid's Lemma (uniqueness).

registry_objects.title: Split-Complex Forced
registry_objects.summary: The bipolar prime partition forces split-complex (j^2 = +1) over elliptic (i^2 = -1) scalars. Three arguments: bipolar encoding requirement, wave-type propagation, diagonal-discipline compatibility.

registry_objects.title: Minimal Alphabet Theorem
registry_objects.summary: |Gen| = 5 is the unique cardinality achieving completeness (all 3 rewiring levels have channels), rigidity (no non-trivial rho-automorphism), and saturation (tetration has no channel). 4 generators fail completeness; 6 generators fail rigidity.

registry_objects.title: Six-Generator Rigidity Failure
registry_objects.summary: A 6-generator tau-like system admits a non-trivial rho-automorphism: the swap eta <-> zeta commutes with rho6 and is an involution, yet is not the identity. This breaks rigidity.

registry_objects.title: Four-Generator Ladder Incompleteness
registry_objects.summary: With 4 generators, only 2 solenoidal generators (pi, gamma) exist for 3 rewiring levels needed. Exponentiation has no canonical channel. This breaks ladder completeness.

registry_objects.title: Tetration Algebraic Degradation
registry_objects.summary: Tetration is algebraically degraded: non-commutative (2^^3 != 3^^2), non-associative ((2^^2)^^2 != 2^^(2^^2)), no left identity >= 2. This is the algebraic obstruction to canonicality at the 4th operation level.

registry_objects.title: Spectral Decomposition
registry_objects.summary: Every element of L decomposes uniquely into B-sector and C-sector components via characters. The profinite topology on Z_hat_tau provides the convergence framework.

registry_objects.title: Explosion Barrier
registry_objects.summary: In Truth4, B = 'both true and false' does NOT cause explosion (ex falso quodlibet). B-witnesses and not-B-witnesses live in different spectral sectors. Structural theorem, not axiom choice.

registry_objects.title: No Additive Inverse
registry_objects.summary: For n > 0, no m in tau-Idx satisfies n + m = 0. The absence of additive inverses is structural: rho generates positive depths only.

registry_objects.title: No Ring Negation
registry_objects.summary: No function neg: tau-Idx -> tau-Idx satisfies n + neg(n) = 0 for all n. tau-Idx is a commutative semiring but not a ring.

registry_objects.title: Mul Cancel Fails at Zero
registry_objects.summary: 0 * 1 = 0 * 2 but 1 != 2. Multiplicative left-cancellation fails when the cancelled factor is zero.

registry_objects.title: Multiplicative Cancellation iff Positive
registry_objects.summary: CLIMAX: Multiplicative cancellation holds for n iff n > 0. Zero is the unique obstruction. One locus, one guard, maximal universality everywhere else.

registry_objects.title: CRT Coherence Constraint
registry_objects.summary: Tower-coherent functions that are well-defined on Z/M_kZ depend only on the CRT residue at stage k. Proved concretely for chi_plus and chi_minus; the general case requires residue-respect as hypothesis.

registry_objects.title: Diagonal-Free Protection
registry_objects.summary: The zero-divisor product e_plus * e_minus = 0 cannot arise as T(t1) * T(t2) for any T in HolFun and compatible omega-tails t1, t2. Sector-pure outputs cannot combine nontrivially.

registry_objects.title: Composition Closure
registry_objects.summary: HolFun is closed under composition: if f1 and f2 are tower-coherent reduce-form functions, then f1 o f2 is tower-coherent. Proven via reduction_compat on composed reduce-form functions.

registry_objects.title: Tau-Identity Theorem
registry_objects.summary: THE CROWN JEWEL: if two tau-holomorphic functions agree at stage d0 for all inputs, they agree at all stages <= d0. Hallmark of holomorphic rigidity. Proof uses tower coherence for vertical propagation (not classical sideways analytic continuation).

registry_objects.title: Category Axioms
registry_objects.summary: Cat_tau satisfies the category axioms: left/right identity for stagewise composition (id_stage), and associativity of composition (stagefun_comp_assoc). All proven from HolFun monoid properties.

registry_objects.title: Yoneda Lemma
registry_objects.summary: The Yoneda Lemma for thin Cat_tau: natural transformations from y(X) to presheaf P are in bijection with P(X). In the thin setting this simplifies to: evaluation at X determines the transformation.

registry_objects.title: Grothendieck Topos
registry_objects.summary: PSh(Cat_tau) is a Grothendieck topos. Standard result: for any small category C, PSh(C) is a Grothendieck topos. Cat_tau is small (countable objects, thin morphisms). Verified via terminal object, products, and identity laws.

registry_objects.title: Omega_tau Subobject Classifier
registry_objects.summary: Omega_tau = Truth4 is the subobject classifier for PSh(Cat_tau). Every truth value is one of T, F, B, N. The four elements are pairwise distinct (omega_tau_card_four). Previewed in Part XI, now EARNED.

registry_objects.title: Product Universal Property
registry_objects.summary: Product universal property: if R maps to both P and Q pointwise, then R maps to P x Q. Also: product is commutative, associative, and unital (with terminal presheaf).

registry_objects.title: Distributivity
registry_objects.summary: Product distributes over coproduct: P x (Q v R) = (P x Q) v (P x R). Both left and right distributivity hold. This makes (E_tau, x, v) a distributive category.

registry_objects.title: Cartesian Closed
registry_objects.summary: E_tau is cartesian closed: Hom(A x B, C) <-> Hom(A, C^B) pointwise. The evaluation morphism (Q^P x P) -> Q is verified. Internal hom with terminal/initial satisfies expected identities.

registry_objects.title: Spectral Determination
registry_objects.summary: Spectral Determination: two StageFuns with identical spectral coefficients at all inputs and stages are equal. The spectral decomposition is faithful.

registry_objects.title: Removable Singularity
registry_objects.summary: Removable Singularity: two tower-coherent functions agreeing at depth d0 for all inputs agree at all depths <= d0. Repackaging of the Identity Theorem in extension language. The thin set is removable.

registry_objects.title: Global Hartogs Extension
registry_objects.summary: THE BOOK I CLIMAX. Global Hartogs Extension: any two tower-coherent functions agreeing at a reference depth agree at all depths below. Uses all four ingredients: spectral determination, CRT extension, tower coherence, and the Identity Theorem.

registry_objects.title: Cantor Diagonal Inapplicability
registry_objects.summary: Cantor diagonal argument is inapplicable in tau: the three prerequisites (unrestricted decimal expansion, unrestricted comprehension, free Cartesian diagonal) all fail within the earned set theory.

registry_objects.title: Unique Infinity Object
registry_objects.summary: Unique infinity object: omega is the sole infinite object in tau, and all approaches to infinity are mediated by omega-germs on the primorial ladder. No hierarchy of infinities exists; infinity is singular and structural.

registry_objects.title: Diagonal-Linear Correspondence
registry_objects.summary: The diagonal discipline (I.D03) and the structural fragment of !-free linear logic are structurally isomorphic: K5's refusal of self-products corresponds to absence of contraction, channel consumption to one-use-per-formula, saturation to finite linear context, controlled overflow to bounded !-introduction.

registry_objects.title: Linearity Census
registry_objects.summary: Linearity census of TauLib: 75/80 modules fully constructive, 1 module uses Classical.em (eliminable, I.P38), 1 module uses funext tactic (CIC kernel axiom). Book I's formalization is compatible with the !-free fragment of linear logic at the object level.

registry_objects.title: K5 Structural Exclusion
registry_objects.summary: K5 diagonal discipline places tau on star-autonomous side; Lawvere FPT does not apply. Necessary but not sufficient for self-hosting.

registry_objects.title: Presheaf Characterization
registry_objects.summary: HolFun = Nat(F, F_j) ∩ D-Hol: a tau-holomorphic function is a natural transformation from the primorial presheaf to its split-complex extension that satisfies sector independence.

registry_objects.title: Bi-Square Characterization
registry_objects.summary: The complete structural characterization: pasted bi-square of tower coherence (left) and spectral naturality (right). Both squares commute independently; together equivalent to HolFun. Global Hartogs: limit row determines every stage row.

registry_objects.title: Archimedean Property
registry_objects.summary: The Archimedean property: the natural number embedding into TauReal is unbounded and injective. For any n < m, fromNat(m) is not equivalent to fromNat(n).

registry_objects.title: TauComplex Ring Axioms
registry_objects.summary: TauComplex satisfies all commutative ring axioms including i^2=-1. Each axiom reduces through TauReal to TauRat algebra via the toInt bridge.

registry_objects.title: Quaternion Non-Commutativity
registry_objects.summary: The quaternions are non-commutative: qi * qj is not equivalent to qj * qi. Explicit witness: the k-component differs in sign. This is the first non-commutative algebra earned within tau.

registry_objects.title: Roots of Unity CRT Decomposition
registry_objects.summary: CRT decomposition of roots of unity: for coprime moduli m1, m2, a root of unity mod m1*m2 decomposes into roots mod m1 and mod m2. Connects cyclotomic structure to the CRT basis that pervades the spectral theory.

registry_objects.title: Ontic Identity Invariance
registry_objects.summary: Ontic Identity Invariance: in the coherence kernel (K0-K6), every admissible construction preserves ontic identity. The normalization map to canonical form is unique and path-independent; no construction can introduce alternative identity witnesses or partial identifications.

registry_objects.title: Slippage Breaks Unique Omega
registry_objects.summary: Slippage Breaks Unique Omega: any foundational stack permitting identity slippage at the substrate level cannot internalize a unique absolute infinity omega. It can only generate many infinities (model-relative, non-canonical) via limit/quotient constructions. Explains why ZFC has aleph_0, aleph_1, ... while tau has one omega.

registry_objects.title: Structural Instability Theorem
registry_objects.summary: Structural Instability Theorem: diagonal-resonant foundations cannot host identity-faithful reception of tau. The L+E+P components jointly create identity slack preventing any global projection from preserving distinctness. Not inconsistency — structural incompatibility with tau ontic granularity.

registry_objects.title: Countable Additivity
registry_objects.summary: The stage-k counting measure is finitely additive: for disjoint subsets S, T of Z/M_k Z, μ_k(S ∪ T) = μ_k(S) + μ_k(T). Verified computationally at stage 3 for even/odd and B/C sector partitions.

registry_objects.title: Fundamental Theorem of Internal Galois Theory
registry_objects.summary: Every unit of Z/M_k Z generates a valid ring automorphism preserving both addition and multiplication. This gives a bijection between units and automorphisms, the τ-internal Galois correspondence.

registry_objects.title: Linearity of Integration
registry_objects.summary: The τ-integral is linear: ∫_k (af + bg) = a ∫_k f + b ∫_k g. Verified computationally for arbitrary coefficients at stage 2.

registry_objects.title: Canonical Normalisation (Hinge 7)
registry_objects.summary: Every admissible code c in Code reduces in finitely many witness-preserving tau-kernel rewriting steps ->_NF to a unique normal form NF(c) in Code^NF. The normalisation map NF: Code -> Code^NF is idempotent, surjective, teq-preserving, bounded by pass budget k_0(c) in N. Source: Hinge 7 (address-resolution), main.tex Thm 1.1 + section-03-nf-confluence Thm 3.x.

registry_objects.title: NF Confluence / Church-Rosser for tau-kernel (Hinge 7)
registry_objects.summary: The tau-kernel rewriting system (Code, ->_NF) is confluent (Church-Rosser): for every c in Code and every pair c ->* c_1, c ->* c_2, there exists a common reduct c' with c_1 ->* c' and c_2 ->* c'. Diamond property; every teq-class has unique NF representative. Proved via strong normalisation + local confluence + Newman's Lemma. THIS DISCHARGES the 'modulo Hinge 7 NF confluence' scope caveats of Hinge 5 Thm 1.8 (pre-Yoneda collapse) and Hinge 6 Thm 1.1 (topos structure) + Thm 1.3 (circularity resolution). Source: Hinge 7 section-03 Thm 3.x.

registry_objects.title: Genealogical DAG Structure (Hinge 7)
registry_objects.summary: The pair DAG := (Code, ->_NF) is a countable, strongly-normalising, finite-width directed acyclic graph: acyclic via well-founded measure, SN bounded by pass budget k_0, finite-width polynomial in primorial M_k, unique root c_empty, one NF sink per teq-class. Sinks(DAG)/teq = AddrTau. Source: Hinge 7 section-05-dag.

registry_objects.title: Cayley Word Metric (Hinge 7)
registry_objects.summary: The Cayley word metric d_Cay on the DAG, defined as minimal n_1 + n_2 over common reducts, is a genuine metric on AddrTau = Code^NF/teq (reflexive, symmetric, triangle inequality, separation modulo teq). Coincides with Hinge 1's minimal-pass distance. Integer-valued; induces the tau-topology on AddrTau. Effective Bourdon dimension bounded by primorial growth. Source: Hinge 7 section-06-cayley.

registry_objects.title: Ontic Ultrametric (Hinge 7)
registry_objects.summary: The Cayley-completion (Ultra, d_inf) = widehat{(AddrTau, d_Cay')} is a complete ultrametric space: strong triangle inequality d_inf(a,c) <= max(d_inf(a,b), d_inf(b,c)), non-archimedean, totally disconnected. Matches the Hinge 4 profinite boundary topology under the primorial ladder (M_k). Ontic (not epistemic) indeterminacy at unstabilised addresses. iota_tau anchors the scale via sigma-fixed endomorphism orbit. This is the tau-native replacement for Euclidean distance in Books II-VII. Source: Hinge 7 section-07-ultrametric.

registry_objects.title: Address Resolution and Absence of Equations (Hinge 7)
registry_objects.summary: Every tau-native equality question a = b reduces to a finite-witness decidable NF comparison NF(a) == NF(b); decidable in polynomial depth. Consequently, Category tau has NO equations in the classical sense: only codes, canonical addresses, and the NF-resolution procedure. Classical equational view emerges as extensional shadow via faithful-but-not-full functor Shad: Cat_tau -> Eq-Alg. Fullness is blocked by DD1-DD4 diagonal discipline (Hinge 5). Source: Hinge 7 section-08-address-resolution.

registry_objects.title: Hinge 7 Integration Tabulation (Bundle Closure)
registry_objects.summary: Hinge 7 is the foundational capstone: (a) discharges modulo-Hinge-7 caveats of Hinges 5-6; (b) supplies canonical-address framework as coordinate primitive for Hinges 1-4; (c) establishes ontic ultrametric as tau-native metric for Books II-VII; (d) closes the 7-hinge foundational arc. The Panta Rhei framework now has a closed, self-contained, seven-hinge bundle of standalone peer-reviewable papers. Source: Hinge 7 main.tex Thm 1.7.

registry_objects.title: Ontic Identity Invariance (Hinge 8)
registry_objects.summary: In the tau-kernel, normalisation to canonical form is unique and path-independent (NF map Norm: Code -> Code^NF). No admissible construction introduces shadow identities. Ontic identity is invariant under admissible symmetries (kernel-axiom-preserving tau-endofunctors). Identity slippage is zero at every primorial-ladder stage. Proved via three independent blockings of diagonal-resonance components L/E/P (KAxiom 5, NF confluence, *-autonomous structure). Source: Hinge 8 (kernel-foundation) main.tex Thm 1.1 + section-06-ontic-identity Thm 6.1; cites Book I Thm I.T46.
